observations: Published Web Forms have root/list/new/name/name-edit routes.
Dynamic route arguments disable page caching.
Website routes include installed-app www and templates/pages files.
clear_routing_cache invalidates published Web Form, dynamic Web Page and home-page caches.
Reverse installed-app precedence chooses existing static HTML/Markdown/index route.
Template context includes controller get_context, frontmatter, sidebar/breadcrumbs and colocated JS/CSS.
get_html is decorated with cache_html; rendered response adds CSRF token.
Portal Settings composes standard/custom menu items and default home.
Updating Portal Settings invalidates website and user/role home-page caches.
get_portal_sidebar_items filters enabled menu entries by actor role.
Portal sidebar cache is keyed by session user.
clear_cache invalidates routing, HTML/page and portal/menu/home-page data.
Web Form self-service read/write applies owner, website permission or DocPerm according to settings.
allow_edit guards accept updates; allow_delete and session ownership guard deletion.
Authenticated submissions normally retain session owner; anonymous forms temporarily use Guest.
Published form routing data uses a one-hour Redis cache.

behavior: Every conditional read resolves the current tenant and publication state first.
SHA256 validator covers trusted tenant id, API pathname and complete public representation.
Browser cache must revalidate; shared caching is disabled with private cache control.
Full public page/navigation/theme/preset changes invalidate validators.
Unpublishing and lookup errors cannot revive cached public content.
forge_cache_slice.classification: bounded observable invalidation behavior; different implementation from Redis/HTML cache

remaining_gap: Dynamic and nested website/web-form route matching and rendering remain absent in flat-slug client routing.

Installed-app HTML/Markdown/Jinja templates, frontmatter, controller context and colocated assets remain unsupported; arbitrary Python context execution is an intentional architecture/security difference.
Role-filtered Portal Settings menus/home composition is separate from ERPNext customer/supplier business self-service.
Captured upstream runtime fixtures and differential execution are still required for a full closure claim.
scope_note: Customer/supplier ERP business workflows belong to ERPNext comparison, rather than being implied by the Frappe framework denominator's portal permission behavior.
